summary: The sole AC ('No prompt-only (mechanisable) line is left unaddressed anywhere in the ledger') holds when walked concretely. I grepped the post-diff ledger myself: exactly 3 literal `prompt-only (mechanisable)` occurrences remain, matching the diff's own re-measurement (3) rather than a rounder claim, and the sibling count I spot-checked (31 `prompt-only (judgement)`) matches too, so the accounting is measured, not asserted. Each of the 3 is accounted for and verified in-file, not merely claimed: line 15 is the legend's own status-definition row, line 1820 is the historical 2026-07-26 end-check distribution table (both prose, neither a live criterion row promising product behaviour), and line 531 is FR-01.06 #6b, which carries an explicit reason plus a filed follow-up (`trg-2f7a840a`) from the earlier e3 sub-iterate — I read that row and confirmed it, rather than trusting the 'already reconciled' summary. These two non-row occurrences are precisely the spec's own named 'preamble and end-check strays', so the scope statement and the outcome agree. The one genuine criterion row, FR-01.14 #1, is addressed by building the oracle the row itself named ('a meta-test over the call sites') rather than a near-neighbour: `shared/scripts/lib/triage_plain_append_scan.py` + `triage_plain_append_scope.py` with a caller allowlist and a reverse-drift guard in `shared/tests/test_triage_append_producer_registry.py`. I verified the row's cited evidence exists and the numbers reconcile: 5 registry cases and 18 scanner cases across the three sibling test files (23 total, matching the declared `test_completeness` count), and the reverse-guard proofs call the live `_assert_registry_matches` path rather than re-typing an assertion, so the guard is shown failing, not merely passing. The status flip to bare `enforced, tested` does not overclaim within this spec's remit: the concurrency half of that criterion was already `enforced, tested` pre-diff via the shared lock critical section, and it is the producer-opt-in half that this unit gates. In-scope throughout — new files plus the ledger/ADR/changelog/metadata artifacts of a checks-only unit, no production behaviour change to triage.py or any producer, consistent with `spec_impact: none` + `affected_frs: [FR-01.14]`. Two notes I am deliberately NOT rejecting on, flagged for Stage 2 rather than swallowed: external review's openai leg twice raised high-severity 'spec' findings that (a) exempting `triage_add.py` and (b) leaving package-qualified/relative imports (`from shared.scripts.triage import append_triage_item`) undetected mean the gate is not airtight. Both are residual-strength questions about the check, not divergences from this spec's text — each gap is named in the module docstrings and the ADR, positively pinned by `test_a_package_qualified_import_is_a_named_accepted_gap`, and justified empirically against the live tree; the other external leg (GLM) approved and specifically found no path by which the registry test passes while the guarantee is broken. Whether those accepted gaps are strong enough engineering is the code-reviewer's and doubt-reviewer's call. Code-reviewer may proceed.
